title: Mercimek Corbasi
subtitle: Turkish red lentil soup with cumin and paprika butter
excerpt: A thick, silky red lentil soup finished with a spiced butter poured over the top. One of the most widely eaten soups in Turkey, served at every meal from breakfast to dinner.
sourceNotes: The red lentil soup that appears on every Turkish table; the spiced butter finish is essential to the dish and should not be skipped.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the soup without the butter finish. Reheat from frozen, then make the butter fresh before serving.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles very easily. Store in the fridge for up to 4 days; thin with a little water when reheating if it thickens.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the soup a day ahead and refrigerate. The spiced butter must be made fresh just before serving.

content.text: Mercimek corbasi is a pureed red lentil soup with a spiced butter poured on top at serving. The soup itself is mild and filling; the butter adds heat and colour. Do not skip the spiced butter: it is half the dish.
Heat the olive oil in the large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion and carrot. Cook for 8 minutes until soft and beginning to colour.
Add the garlic, cumin, sweet paprika, and tomato puree. Stir for 2 minutes.
Add the rinsed lentils and pour in the stock. Stir well. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until the lentils are completely soft and broken down.
Take the pan off the heat. Blend the soup smooth with a stick blender. Season with salt and pepper. Add a little more stock or water if it is too thick.

Return to a low heat while you make the spiced butter. Melt the butter in the small saucepan over a medium heat. When it foams, add the hot paprika and dried mint. Swirl for 30 seconds. Remove from the heat.
Ladle the soup into bowls. Drizzle the spiced butter over each portion. Add a squeeze of lemon and serve immediately.

items.symptom: The soup is gritty rather than smooth.
items.cause: The lentils were not cooked long enough, or the blending was too brief.
items.fix: Simmer for another 10 minutes until the lentils are fully collapsed, then blend again for at least 1 full minute.

items.symptom: The soup is too thick after blending.
items.fix: Thin with hot water or stock a ladleful at a time until you reach a creamy, pourable consistency.

items.symptom: The butter burns before the paprika blooms.
items.fix: Use a medium heat and watch carefully. The butter should foam gently. Remove from the heat as soon as the paprika colour bleeds into the butter.
